title: Rupture Disc

introduction.definition: A rupture (bursting) disc is a non-reclosing pressure-relief device: a thin membrane that bursts at a specified pressure and temperature, instantly opening a relief path. It reacts in milliseconds and is leak-tight before bursting, so it is used for rapid pressure rise, toxic/corrosive service, or under a safety valve to protect it.
applications: Upstream of safety valves (isolation from corrosive fluid)
key_points: One-shot: must be replaced after bursting
Burst pressure has a tolerance and depends on temperature

classification.type: Forward-acting, scored domed disc in holder

introduction.summary: A rupture (bursting) disc is a non-reclosing pressure-relief device: a thin metal membrane designed to burst at a specified pressure and temperature, opening a full relief path in milliseconds. It is used alone where fast, leak-tight relief is needed, or upstream of a safety valve to isolate it from corrosive process fluid.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Install with the flow arrow towards the outlet; never upside down.
Where a disc is below a safety valve, monitor the space between them (telltale gauge).
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

periodic.task: Replace discs on a planned interval (fatigue, corrosion).

overhaul.task: Inspect holder seating surfaces when replacing.

lubrication: None — do not grease seating faces.

causes: Fatigue from pressure cycling, corrosion, damaged on handling

video_tutorials.title: Rupture Disc — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Rupture Disc.
A rupture (bursting) disc is a non-reclosing pressure-relief device: a thin membrane that bursts at a specified pressure and temperature, instantly opening a relief path.
It reacts in milliseconds and is leak-tight before bursting, so it is used for rapid pressure rise, toxic/corrosive service, or under a safety valve to protect it.
Typical applications include reactors and pressure vessels; upstream of safety valves (isolation from corrosive fluid); compressed-gas systems; dust explosion venting (vent panels).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Disc Holder (inlet & outlet rings) with Tag.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Rupture Disc — Operation

script.narration: How the Rupture Disc works.
The disc is clamped in its holder between flanges.
As system pressure rises, the domed disc is strained.
At burst pressure it tears along the score lines into petals.
The petals fold open and the full bore relieves the pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Upstream (red) the system pressure rises; downstream (blue) is the relief line at near-atmospheric pressure.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rupture Disc.
Check telltale gauge/burst indicator.
Replace discs on a planned interval (fatigue, corrosion).
Inspect holder seating surfaces when replacing.
Watch for premature burst: burst below set pressure. Common cause: fatigue from pressure cycling, corrosion, damaged on handling.
Watch for failure to burst at set: overpressure. Common cause: installed upside down, wrong disc.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
